paper_scope: A differentiable HiGS training method with a native CUDA backward and hierarchy-aware sparse/progressive training.

contributions.statement: A native differentiable HiGS backward with explicit gradient and topology-lifecycle contracts.
A hierarchy-aware sparse and progressive training method that reduces end-to-end training cost.
A reproducible analysis of speed, quality, memory, and failure modes across scene scales.

claims.statement: The tracked A100 R60 short-horizon, pretrained-Ply artifact contains three-seed aggregate groups for Train, Garden, and Bicycle under the masked-Adam study.
The proposed method reduces complete training wall time while matching final full-training quality across standard datasets.
claims.blocking_gate: The executed 177-job matrix shows final PSNR below the same-backend gsplat control on 10 of 11 scenes and aggregate time-to-quality 4.3% above the control; a quality-preserving wall-time reduction was not observed.

claims.statement: A frozen 177-job A100 full-training matrix executed end-to-end with zero failed or missing jobs (original_3dgs 33, gsplat 48, higs_full 48, higs_proposed 48); the proposed method trains from SfM initialization with lower mean peak GPU memory than the gsplat control (2.79 vs 3.72 GiB; mean per-job reduction 21.6%).
The method outperforms current training accelerators under their official implementations and matched quality targets.
claims.blocking_gate: Evaluate official Speedy-Splat, Turbo-GS, random-tile, standard 3DGS, and gsplat training paths; proxy-style reimplementations are ablations, not headline baselines.

claims.statement: The training improvement generalizes beyond the A100 cohort.
claims.blocking_gate: Repeat the frozen training matrix on at least one consumer GPU and one additional data-center architecture, reporting separate cohorts.
